title: Right Kan extension of a constant space along a right fibration
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent transformations and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], spaces $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], and coherent fiber transport of [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $p:E\to B$ be a right fibration of $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories: $p$ lifts every $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$. Let $Q_p:B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ be its contravariant fiber transport; $Q_p(b)$ is the Kan fiber $E_b$, and $g:b\to b'$ acts by lifting $g$ with prescribed target in $E_{b'}$. For a $\mathcal U$-small space $X$ let $R_X:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ be the coherent functor $R_X(b)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}(Q_p(b),X)$, with $R_X(g)$ given by precomposition with $Q_p(g)$, using the coherent Hom functor of [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]. Evaluation at a point $e\in E_b=Q_p(b)$ defines a coherent transformation $\epsilon_X:R_Xp\to\Delta_E X$. For every coherent $F:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, the map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(F,R_X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(E,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(Fp,\Delta_E X),\qquad\theta\longmapsto\epsilon_X(\theta p)$$
is an equivalence of whole spaces. At $e\in E_b$ its image has component $x\mapsto\theta_b(x)(e)$. The transformation $\epsilon_X$ is the counit exhibiting $R_X$ as the right Kan extension of $\Delta_E X$ along $p$. The formula and equivalence are natural in $F,X$ with coherent simplicial parameters retained. Empty fibers and empty $E$ are allowed; functor categories are formed in a containing universe.

source.place: Opposite dual of Kerodon Propositions 7.3.4.1 and 7.3.4.4 (fiberwise Kan extension along a cartesian fibration), and Proposition 7.3.6.1 (0309, mapping-space universal property). Right fibrations have groupoidal fibers, so the fiberwise limit of the constant space X is Map(E_b,X), with evaluation counit. Read online; archival copy WANTED. Kerodon tags are not Stacks tags; no Stacks theorem for quasicategories.

proof.text: Construction of $\epsilon_X$. Let $p':E\times_BE\to E$ be the projection to the first factor, the pullback of $p$ along $p$. It is a right fibration in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]: a lifting problem for $\Lambda^n_i\subseteq\Delta^n$ ($n\geq1$, $0<i\leq n$) against $p'$ is solved by solving its second coordinate against $p$, the first coordinate being prescribed. Its fibre over $e\in E_b$ is $\{e\}\times E_b=E_b$. The diagonal $\delta=(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id}):E\to E\times_BE$ is a section of $p'$, that is, a vertex of $\Gamma(p')$. By [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit], evaluation of sections is a cone $\Gamma(p')\to m_{p'}$; composing it with the vertex $\delta:\Delta^0\to\Gamma(p')$ gives a coherent transformation $\tau':\Delta_{E^{\mathrm{op}}}\Delta^0\to m_{p'}$ whose component at $e$ is the point $\delta(e)=e$ of the fibre $E_{p(e)}$. The naturality of transport under restriction of the base, in the same statement, identifies $m_{p'}$ coherently with $Q_p\circ p^{\mathrm{op}}$, compatibly with the fibre identifications above; so $\tau'$ becomes a coherent transformation $\tau:\Delta_{E^{\mathrm{op}}}\Delta^0\to Q_pp^{\mathrm{op}}$ whose component at $e$ is the tautological point $e\in Q_p(p(e))$.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 7.3.4.1 (02ZL), opposite form, as the target of the comparison; the evaluation transformation is the tautological section of the pulled-back right fibration composed with the Hom functor (agent-written).

proof.text: Apply the coherent Hom bifunctor $H$ of $\mathcal C=\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ from [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] (with $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ is $\mathcal U'$-small with $\mathcal U$-small mapping spaces) in its contravariant first variable, with second variable $X$. This gives a coherent transformation $H(\tau,X):H(Q_pp(-),X)\to H(\Delta^0,X)$ of functors $E\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. Its source is $R_Xp$ by the definition of $R_X$. Its target is the constant diagram at $H(\Delta^0,X)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}(\Delta^0,X)$, which [lem-coef-space-constant-diagram-limit] for $K=\Delta^0$ identifies with $X$ (a limit of a diagram on one vertex is its value), the identification being evaluation at the vertex. Call the resulting transformation $\epsilon_X:R_Xp\to\Delta_EX$. The first-variable action of $H$ is precomposition, so the component of $\epsilon_X$ at $e\in E_b$ sends $x\in\operatorname{Map}(Q_p(b),X)$ to $x\circ e=x(e)$. Since $H$ is a coherent functor of both variables, $\epsilon_X$ is natural in $X$, with all simplicial parameters. On a fibre $K=E_b$, the diagonal section is the identity of $K$. Consequently, under the evaluation-cone identification in [lem-coef-space-constant-diagram-limit], the restriction of this construction is evaluation on every simplex: an $n$-parameter map $u:K\times\Delta^n\to X$ evaluated on $s:\Delta^n\to K$ is $t\mapsto u(s(t),t)$. Restriction along $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ gives $u(s(\alpha(t)),\alpha(t))$ in either order. Thus the restricted cone is the specified coherent evaluation cone, including its higher data, rather than merely a cone with the same vertex components.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 7.3.4.1 (02ZL), opposite form, as the target of the comparison; the evaluation transformation is the tautological section of the pulled-back right fibration composed with the Hom functor (agent-written).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-right-fibration-fiberwise-kan] to $p$ and $G=\Delta_EX$. Each restricted diagram $G_b=\Delta_{E_b}X$ has a limit by [lem-coef-space-constant-diagram-limit], applied to the Kan complex $E_b$ (also when $E_b=\varnothing$). The node gives a coherent functor $\operatorname{Ran}_pG:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ and a counit $\eta:(\operatorname{Ran}_pG)p\to G$ whose restriction to each $E_b$ is a limiting cone on $G_b$, and for every coherent $F:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ an equivalence of spaces $\Phi_F:\operatorname{Map}(F,\operatorname{Ran}_pG)\to\operatorname{Map}(Fp,\Delta_EX)$, $\phi\mapsto\eta\circ(\phi p)$, natural in $F$.

source.place: Kerodon Propositions 7.3.4.1 and 7.3.4.4 (02ZL) in opposite form, with Proposition 7.3.6.1 (0309) for the mapping-space property.

proof.text: Take $F=R_X$ in Step 3. Since $\Phi_{R_X}$ is an equivalence of Kan complexes, it is surjective on components. Choose an edge $\alpha:R_X\to\operatorname{Ran}_pG$ whose image is in the component of $\epsilon_X$ from Step 2. The Kan property supplies a path $h:\eta\circ(\alpha p)\simeq\epsilon_X$ in $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(E,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(R_Xp,\Delta_EX)$. This uses the Kan mapping-space assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]; no equality of chosen composites is asserted.

source.place: Kerodon Propositions 7.3.4.1 and 7.3.4.4 (02ZL) in opposite form, with Proposition 7.3.6.1 (0309) for the mapping-space property.

proof.text: Fix $b\in B$ and put $K=E_b$, $G_b=\Delta_KX$. Restriction of $R_Xp$ to $K$ is constant with value $R_X(b)=\operatorname{Map}(K,X)$, and restriction of $\alpha p$ is constant at $\alpha_b$. By Step 2 the restricted $\epsilon_X$ is the evaluation cone, including higher simplices, which is limiting by [lem-coef-space-constant-diagram-limit]. The restricted $\eta$ is limiting by Step 3. Restrict the path $h$ of Step 4 to $K$. The pair $(\alpha_b,h|_K)$ is a point in the homotopy fiber over $\epsilon_X|_K$ of the map sending an apex map $a$ to $\eta|_K\circ\Delta_Ka$. By the cone mapping-space assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], this fiber is equivalent to the space of morphisms between these cones in $(\Delta_K\downarrow G_b)$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Hence it supplies a cone morphism with apex map in the component of $\alpha_b$. Both cones are terminal. The terminal-object subcategory is Kan by the same calculus node, so that morphism is an equivalence; the apex projection carries its inverse witnesses to inverse witnesses. Thus the component of $\alpha_b$ is invertible. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], an edge has invertible component class precisely when it is an equivalence. Therefore every $\alpha_b$ is an equivalence, including empty $K$, where both apices are terminal. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], $\alpha$ is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$.

source.place: Kerodon Remark 7.1.2.6 (03F3) and Example 7.1.2.9 (03F7): the evaluation cone exhibits Fun(K,X) as the limit of the constant diagram; uniqueness of limits (agent-written).

proof.text: For every coherent $F:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, consider the displayed map $\Psi_F:\theta\mapsto\epsilon_X\circ(\theta p)$. The functoriality of restriction along $p$, the path $h$ of Step 4, and the canonical composition homotopies of the coherent Hom bifunctors of $\operatorname{Fun}(E,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ (formed in a containing universe, [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]) give a homotopy $\Psi_F\simeq\Phi_F\circ\alpha_*$, where $\alpha_*:\operatorname{Map}(F,R_X)\to\operatorname{Map}(F,\operatorname{Ran}_pG)$ is the second-variable action of the Hom bifunctor on $\alpha$. As $\alpha$ is an equivalence edge (Step 5) and a coherent functor carries an equivalence edge with its inverse witnesses to an equivalence, $\alpha_*$ is a homotopy equivalence; $\Phi_F$ is one by Step 3. Hence $\Psi_F$, homotopic to their composite, is an equivalence of whole spaces. Its value at $\theta$ has component at $e\in E_b$ equal to $\epsilon_{X,e}\circ\theta_b$, which by Step 2 is $x\mapsto\theta_b(x)(e)$. So $\epsilon_X$ has the universal property of a counit exhibiting $R_X$ as the right Kan extension of $\Delta_EX$ along $p$ (and it is the counit $\eta$ transported along $\alpha$).

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 7.3.6.1 (0309), opposite form: the mapping-space universal property of the Kan extension, transported along the equivalence alpha.

proof.text: Naturality in $F$ is the first-variable naturality of the Hom bifunctors; naturality in $X$ follows from that of $\epsilon_X$ (Step 2) and the second-variable naturality, with all simplicial parameters. If $E=\varnothing$, every fibre is empty, $\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})=\Delta^0$ and each $R_X(b)$ is terminal; the argument above applies unchanged and both sides are contractible. If $B=\varnothing$, then $E=\varnothing$ and both functor categories have a unique empty diagram. If $p=\mathrm{id}_B$, the fibres are points and the formula gives $R_X\simeq\Delta_BX$ with its evaluation counit. For $B=\Delta^0$ and arbitrary Kan $E=K$, it is precisely the evaluation limit of [lem-coef-space-constant-diagram-limit], including $K=S^1$ and $X=\varnothing$. All domains indexing products or evaluation are $\mathcal U$-small; the functor categories themselves lie in a containing universe.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 7.3.6.1 (0309), opposite form: the mapping-space universal property of the Kan extension, transported along the equivalence alpha.

The statement is unchanged and true: a right fibration is cartesian with Kan fibers, so its right Kan extension is the fiberwise limit Map(E_b,X), with the evaluation counit going R_X p -> Delta_E X. Kerodon 02ZL/0309 (opposite form) and 03F3/03F7 are not in literature/, so I did not read them at the cited places; the proof is marked agent-written and an archival copy is still WANTED. I checked E empty, B empty, p=id, B=pt with K=S^1 or two points, X empty, and empty fibers. Step 1: the pullback of p along p is a right fibration (I checked the lift), and the diagonal section with section-limit's cone and base-restriction naturality gives tau. Step 2: H(tau,X) has the right variance, H(Delta^0,X)=X by evaluation, and the parameter formula identifies the fiber restriction with the evaluation cone. Step 3: fiberwise-kan's fiber-limit hypothesis is discharged by constant-diagram-limit, empty fibers included. Step 4: alpha and the path h come from Kan mapping spaces. Step 5: on each fiber, alpha p restricts to the constant alpha_b; cone-calculus's homotopy fiber turns this into a morphism between terminal cones, so alpha_b is an equivalence, then mapping-composition and pointwise-equivalences make alpha one. One small gap: cone-calculus does not say outright that its equivalence lies over Map(x,y); a Yoneda argument closes it. Step 6: Psi_F is homotopic to Phi_F composed with alpha_*. Step 7: naturality and edge cases hold. There are no new nodes, no cycle (checked by script), proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses, the TeX is clean and there is no SGA citation. The only off-unit statement is lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus, declared and already in the node's tool_uses; I accept it as a generic tool. No fixes, no nodes dropped.
